---
title: Remote work policy
department: people
status: current
---
Northwind roles are classified as site based, hybrid or fully remote at the point
the role is opened, and the classification appears in the job advertisement. A
classification is a property of the role and not a privilege granted to an
individual, so it does not change when a manager changes.

Site based roles are those that cannot be done anywhere else: depot operations,
driving, engineering work on physical equipment. Hybrid roles attend a named site
at least eight days per month. Fully remote roles have no attendance requirement
and no expectation of living within travelling distance of a site.

Hybrid attendance is measured monthly, not weekly, so an employee may attend in
concentrated blocks. Managers may set a fixed team day, and where they do it is
published a quarter ahead so people can plan around it.

Employees may work from another country for up to thirty calendar days per year
without approval beyond their manager, provided they have the right to work
there. Beyond thirty days the arrangement creates a tax presence for the company
and requires people team and finance approval.

Home working equipment is provided by the company: a laptop, a monitor, a
keyboard and a chair. Employees may claim a one off allowance towards a desk.
Ongoing utility costs are not reimbursed and this is deliberate, because
attempting to apportion a household bill creates more work than it returns.

Meetings default to fully remote friendly. Where any attendee is remote, everyone
joins from their own device rather than clustering around one room microphone.
This costs the people in the room a little and saves the remote attendees a lot.

Changing the classification of an existing role requires a business case
reviewed by the people team, and the review considers whether the change would
exclude anyone currently doing the job.
